segments: 125 {OCR?} ... men with heavy taxes,
and he gathered all the silver and gold into his treasury.
And when men were distressed,
they were digging up graves, perhaps they might find jewels that were buried with the dead.
And at that time, also in the city of Nicomedia, the Romans dug,
and they found a cave in which was placed Nicodemus (Nicomedes?) who built it,
being embalmed,
and with him jewels of gold,
and rubies (hyacinths?) that shone in the darkness.
And when the emperor Constantine noticed it,
he showed magnanimity,
and took nothing at all from there.
For he said:
"It is shameful for those who are alive to be in need of the dead."
Instead, he sent artisans,
and very strongly sealed up the place;
and they heaped a great mountain of earth and stones over it.
And at that time there was a pestilence in Syria and Assyria,
and a tormenting famine,
not by reason of a lack of wheat,
but for the reason that no one had any zuz remaining.
The price of an ox or a donkey was one zuz,
and ten measures of wine for one zuz,
and five mudds of wheat for one zuz;
boys and girls for five zuzes each.
And after thirty years of these chastisements, Abu Ja'far died at the Kaaba (or Ka'batha?),
and the world was relieved of distress.
And twenty-five days before his death, Constantine also, the emperor of the Romans, departed this life;
and his son Leo reigned for five years.
At this time, George son of Bukhtishu' the Elamite was distinguished in the art of medicine.
The Caliph al-Mansur sent and brought him from Elam to Baghdad,
that he might heal him of a stomach disease that he had.
And when he entered before him,
he offered prayers for the Caliph in Persian and in Arabic, in a most elegant manner of speech.
And the Caliph marveled at him,
and made him sit down,
and told him about his illness.
And that physician promised him health by stages,
which also came to pass.
And it is said
that on one of the days, this George entered to the Caliph,
and it was the Feast of the Nativity of our Lord.
And the Caliph said to him:
"What did you eat?" And he replied:
"All good things, as our Lord willed."
And the Caliph said:
"I have heard that you have no wife."
And the physician said:
"Yes, I have an old, feeble woman who is not able to stand on her feet."
